cards.text: The LORD has just warned Israel not to follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan (Leviticus 18:3). Now He tells Moses, Israel's leader, to speak to the whole congregation of Israel. And He opens with a BIG one: be holy.

cards.question: God tells the whole congregation of Israel to be holy. What reason does He give?

answers.text: Because the LORD their God is holy
Because the nations are watching them
Because they are about to enter the land

cards.text: Then God brings it close to home with a command about respect, and right next to it He says to keep His Sabbaths. Then He adds a line He'll come back to again and again: "I am the LORD your God."

cards.question: Starting close to home, God says each person in Israel must respect his ___ and father.
God tells Israel not to make molten gods for themselves.

cards.text: Next, the peace offering, offered so they'll be accepted, and it can be eaten the day it's sacrificed or the next day. That's a two-day window, friend, and I spent YEARS in a junk drawer.

cards.question: So what must happen to whatever's left of the peace offering on the third day?
If someone eats the peace offering on the third day, God will still accept it.

cards.text: By day three it's tainted, and whoever eats it has profaned what is holy to the LORD and must be cut off from his people.

At harvest time, God says don't reap to the very edges of the field or gather the gleanings, and don't strip the vineyard bare or pick up the fallen grapes. Friend, I have scraped every mixing bowl I ever met CLEAN with this mustache, so this one's a stretch for me.

cards.question: God says not to strip the vineyard bare or gather its fallen grapes. Who does He say to leave them for?

cards.text: Now God turns to how His people treat each other: no stealing, no lying, no deceiving one another.

cards.question: Swearing falsely by God's name would ___ His name.
God says no defrauding or robbing a neighbor. And a hired hand's wages? When must he be paid?

answers.text: By the end of the week

cards.text: No holding a worker's pay overnight, friend, so no "the check's in the mail." Then God speaks up for the deaf and the blind.

cards.question: God says it's okay to put a stumbling block before the blind as long as they can't tell who did it.

cards.text: No stumbling blocks, and no cursing the deaf either. Instead, God says to fear Him.

cards.question: In court, God says the poor should get a little extra favor.

cards.text: God says no partiality to the poor and no favoritism to the rich. Every neighbor gets judged fairly.

cards.question: God tells Israel not to go around spreading slander among their people.

cards.text: That covers the group chat with one person conveniently left out, friend. God also says don't endanger your neighbor's life.

cards.question: God says not to harbor hatred against your brother in your heart. What does He tell Israel to do with a neighbor right after that?

answers.text: Let it go and say nothing

cards.question: Why does God say to rebuke your neighbor directly?

answers.text: So you won't incur guilt over him
So he will owe you an apology
So it never goes before a judge

cards.text: Then God says no revenge and no grudges against any of their people. A shiny new stamper took my spot on the counter and I spent YEARS in a junk drawer, and if I saw it today, I'd just say, "Teach me your ways."

cards.question: No revenge and no grudges. So what does God call for instead?

answers.text: Keep your distance from your neighbor
Forgive your neighbor once a year

cards.text: God seals that one with "I am the LORD." And loving your neighbor as yourself is the command Jesus later calls the second, right behind loving God (Matthew 22:37-39).
Now God says to keep His statutes, and He gets VERY specific: no crossbreeding two kinds of livestock, and no sowing a field with two kinds of seed.

cards.question: God says clothing made of two kinds of material is fine to wear.

cards.text: Then a hard case. If a man lies carnally with a slave girl promised to another man, God says there must be due punishment, but they are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed. The man must bring a ram to the Tent of Meeting as a guilt offering, and when the priest makes atonement for him, he will be forgiven.
When Israel enters the land and plants fruit trees, the fruit is forbidden for three years. THREE YEARS, friend, and I can't wait five minutes for a batch to cool.

cards.question: When Israel plants fruit trees in the land, the fruit is forbidden for three years. What happens to all the fruit in the fourth year?

answers.text: It is offered to the LORD in praise
It is stored up for a hard year
It is sold to buy more seed

cards.question: God says waiting until the fifth year to eat from their new fruit trees will increase Israel's harvest.

cards.text: Then comes a quick run of don'ts: no eating anything with blood still in it, no divination or sorcery, no cutting their bodies for the dead, no tattoo marks, and no cutting the hair at the sides of the head or clipping the edges of the beard.
Then God says not to defile your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will be prostituted and filled with depravity.
Then God comes back to His Sabbaths and adds reverence for His sanctuary. He also warns Israel not to turn to mediums or spiritists.

cards.question: What does God say happens to people who seek out mediums and spiritists?

answers.text: They will be defiled by them
They will owe the priest a fine

cards.question: Next God turns to the elderly. What does He tell Israel to do in their presence?

answers.text: Wait for them to speak first

cards.question: When a foreigner lives in Israel's land, God says not to oppress him. So how should Israel treat him?

answers.text: As a guest for one season only
As a hired hand on lower wages

cards.question: God says Israel must love the foreigner living among them as themselves. What reason does He give?

cards.text: Then God turns to measuring: no dishonest measures of length, weight or volume. So no "one cup" that's secretly three-quarters, not in Israel and not in my bakery.

cards.question: God wants honest ___ and weights, plus an honest ephah and an honest hin.

cards.text: God wraps it all up: keep all His statutes and all His ordinances, and follow them. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because God isn't done teaching His people to be holy.
